entities.summary:
Lucius Venuleius Montanus Apronianus was a Roman senator of the first century, suffect consul for the nundinium of January to April AD 92 with Qunintus Volusius Saturninus, replacing the emperor Domitian. He played a key role in the Roman Senate during the reign of Domitian, who ruled from AD 81 to AD 96. Montanus Apronianus was a member of the equestrian order, a prestigious social class in ancient Rome.

Montanus Apronianus was instrumental in the governance of Rome during a period of significant turmoil, including the reign of Domitian, who was notorious for his cruelty and paranoia. The senator's involvement in the Roman Senate helped to shape the course of Roman politics and society during this time.

Despite his significance in Roman history, Montanus Apronianus remains a relatively obscure figure, with much of his life and legacy shrouded in mystery.

He was a key figure in the Roman Senate during the late 1st century AD, leaving behind a lasting impact on Roman politics and governance.

This enigmatic figure's life and legacy are a testament to the complexities and nuances of ancient Roman politics and society.
